data.long_meaning: From the Latin 'Oren' meaning 'mountain' and 'tina' meaning 'song'. In Christianity, the name Orentina symbolizes the power and beauty of God's creation. The name Orentina carries the meaning “Oren's song” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Orentina usually hope their child will grow to embody oren's song and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reflection of the beauty and power of God's creation.
data.etymology: Orentina belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Oren's song.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Orentina total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_hebrew.name: אורנטינה
in_hebrew.meaning: מאירה באור אלוהים, אור ה' נגלה עליה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אורנטינה נגזרת מהמילה 'אור' שפירושה אור, ומוסיפה את הסיומת '-נטינה' שיכולה להיות קשורה למילה 'נט' שפירושה מתנה. כך, ניתן לפרש את השם אורנטינה כמתנה של אור אלוהים או כאור ה' הנגלה עליה. השם מופיע ברוח הרעיון של האור הרוחני הנובע מאלוהים, כפי שנאמר בכתובים 'והיה האור הגדול לאור היום ואת הנרות הקטנים לאור הלילה' (בראשית 1:14).

in_greek.name: Ορεντίνα
in_greek.meaning: Φως Θεού, φωτεινή παρουσία του Θεού
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ορεντίνα προέρχεται από τη λατινική λέξη 'orient', που σημαίνει 'ανατολή' ή 'φως'. Στη συνέχεια, διαμορφώθηκε σύμφωνα με τις ελληνικές γραμματικές δομές. Το όνομα συνδέεται με την έννοια του φωτός του Θεού και της πνευματικής φωτεινότητας που προέρχεται από Αυτόν. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, το φως αποτελεί σύμβολο της πνευματικής αλήθειας και της παρουσίας του Θεού, όπως αναφέρεται στο 'Εγώ είμαι το φως του κόσμου' (Ιωάννης 8:12).

in_latin.name: Orentina
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Orentina derivatur a voce Latina 'oriens', quae 'exoriens' seu 'lux' significat. Hoc nomen ad lucem Dei et ad vitam spiritualem illuminatam refertur. In Ecclesia primitiva, lumen saepe pro veritate et Christiana doctrina usurpabatur, ut in Scripturis 'Ego sum lux mundi' (Ioannis 8:12) legitur.

in_english.name: Orentina
in_english.meaning: Shining light of God, illuminated by divine presence
in_english.long_meaning: The name Orentina is derived from Latin and Greek roots, signifying 'shining light' or 'dawn'. It symbolizes the illumination brought by God's presence. Although not directly mentioned in the Bible, the concept of light as divine truth and salvation is prevalent, e.g., 'You are the light of the world' (Matthew 5:14). Historically, names conveying light and spiritual guidance were common in Christian traditions. Orentina embodies the virtues of enlightenment, hope, and spiritual awakening.

data.cultural_impact: The name Orentina carries a sense of strength and beauty, as it is derived from the Latin 'Oren' meaning 'mountain' and 'tina' meaning 'song'. In many cultures, mountains are seen as powerful and sacred symbols of the natural world. The name Orentina also suggests a connection to music and the arts, as 'tina' means 'song'.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Orentina holds deep spiritual significance in the Christian faith. It symbolizes the belief that God's creation is beautiful and powerful, deserving of song and praise. The name Orentina also reminds us of the journey of faith, as we climb the mountains of life's challenges and overcome them through God's grace and guidance. Ultimately, the name Orentina inspires us to lift our voices in song and praise to the Creator of all things.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Orentina, derived from the Latin word "orare" meaning to pray, represents a deep connection to divine communication and spiritual growth. This name embodies the continuous pursuit of seeking God's guidance and wisdom in everyday life.

historical_references.reference: The name Orentina is believed to have originated from the Latin word 'Orentinus', meaning 'mountainous'. This name was likely given to various locations throughout the Roman Empire due to their hilly or mountainous terrain. One such location is the modern-day town of Orentino, located in northern Italy, which was known as 'Orentina' during the Roman period.
historical_references.time_period: Roman Empire (1st century AD - 5th century AD)

historical_references.reference: Another theory suggests that the name Orentina may have been derived from the name of a local saint, Saint Ursula of Cologne. According to legend, Saint Ursula and her companions were traveling to Rome when they were martyred in what is now the town of Orentino. The name of the town may have been derived from the name of the saint, as 'Orentina' could be a derivation of 'Ursula's town'.
